instructions:
GRS Relay carries each tool call to the Agent API of the GoodRelax Scheduler (GRS) page a person has open in a browser. The page holds the only copy of the schedule document; the relay holds none.
Start with agentApiVersion. If a tool answers with the reason pageNotConnected, ask the person to open the address it gives (all of it, the part after # included), open a document there, and press the Agent API button in the page header. A document open in another browser tab or window does not reach the relay and does not move to the relay's page: the person opens the file again in the page at the relay's address. That address changes each time the relay starts.
Before you write, read the notes (readSchema with which 'notes') and pull only the definitions you need with readSchema and defs, for example ['Task', 'Dependency']; without defs readSchema returns a table of contents. For reading only, the column descriptions in the tool answers are enough.
The whole schemas are the resources grs-document.schema.json and grs-commands.schema.json, or readSchema with full true; they are large, so read them only when the parts are not enough.
Read in small pieces: readSearchRows returns one page of the Search Panel as the person sees it (an empty word is the whole outline) and readTableRows does the same for the Delay Diagnostics Report and the Resource List; readDocument leaves out the MSPDI pass-through fields unless you ask, and can be narrowed to some tasks; readStamp is cheap. Write with applyCommands, handing over the stamp you last read as expectedStamp; the whole batch is applied or refused as one.
readDelayDiagnostics only computes: it changes nothing on the screen. To run the Delay Diagnostics on the screen as the person does, call runDelayDiagnostics; to apply its fix proposals as the screen's Fix does, call issueDelayFixes. Say which you did: reading the values is not running them on the screen.
A refusal is a value, not an error: it names the reason and carries the current stamp, never the document. Read again what you need, then retry.
While the person is dragging, typing in place or answering a question, writes are refused; try again shortly.
To save, pass fileName to an export tool: the relay writes into the save folder the person chose in the relay's settings. If the file exists you may be refused with fileExists: ask the person before passing overwrite true, unless they told you not to ask in this conversation. A request to save again under the same name is not permission to replace the file: ask once even then. The old file is kept as .bak. To open a file, call requestOpenFile: the person picks it in their own file window.
The descriptions here use no row ids of the GRS specification; the specification itself is at https://goodrelax.github.io/gr-scheduler/spec-html/

relayRefusals.pageNotConnected: No GRS page is connected to the relay. If the page was connected a moment ago, it is reconnecting by itself (it tries for about 15 s while the relay keeps running): call readStamp again after that, and ask the person only if it still answers pageNotConnected. Ask the person to open {pageUrl} in a browser: the whole address, the part after # included. Then they open the document in that page (a document open in another tab or window does not count) and press the Agent API button in the page header.
relayRefusals.relayTimedOut: {member} did not answer within {seconds} s. Ask the person whether a question or a window is open on the GRS page.

schemaNotes:
GRS JSON notes: the points that are easy to get wrong. The schema descriptions say the same at more length; when they differ, the schema wins.
Times. Every date-time is a wall clock in project.scheduleDataTimeZone (for example UTC+09:00), written YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS to the minute, with no Z and no offset; GRS never converts one.
A date alone (YYYY-MM-DD) is not a date-time: always write the time of day too, for example the start of the working day for a start and its end for a finish.
project.statusDate is read as a day: its time of day moves neither the status line nor the progress line.
Lengths. Durations and lags count working minutes of the document calendar; one working day is project.minutesPerDay minutes, 480 when it is null.
Dependencies. A dependency sits in the dependencies list of the later task and names the earlier task by predecessorUid.
linkType is a number: 0 finish-to-finish, 1 finish-to-start, 2 start-to-finish, 3 start-to-start.
linkLag is in tenths of a minute whatever lagFormat says: one working day of lag is project.minutesPerDay x 10.
Progress. percentComplete follows from the dates: to record progress write actualStart and actualFinish, or stop while the task is unfinished.
New uids. Tasks, resources, assignments and calendars share one counter: a new uid is project.uidHighWaterMark plus 1, and uids are never reused. In one applyCommands batch each create takes the next number, so a later command of the same batch can name it.
Milestones. Task.milestone is the fact; TaskVisual.shapeKind only draws it and must agree with it.
Comment boxes. CommentBox.fontSizePx is the text size of one comment box, 8 to 24 px; null draws 10 px. Change it with setCommentBoxFontSizePx.
Writing. Send applyCommands with the stamp you last read as expectedStamp; the whole batch is applied or refused as one, and a refusal is a value that names the reason.

tools.name: agentApiVersion
tools.description:
The Agent API version, a UTC date-time string in the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.
Read it first.

tools.name: schemaVersion
tools.description:
The version of the GRS JSON format this GRS reads and writes.
The open document carries its own value, which readDocument returns.

tools.name: readSchema
tools.description:
Returns a JSON Schema the relay carries, in parts.
With neither defs nor full it returns a table of contents: the top-level keys and every definition name with one line about it, and the document schema version (schemaVersion).
With defs it returns only those definitions, with the names of the other definitions they refer to; with full true it returns the whole text, the same as the resource grs-document.schema.json or grs-commands.schema.json.
With which 'notes' it returns the short notes to read before writing.
It works even before a page is connected; the schemas are those of the page the relay serves.

which.description: What to read: 'document' is the JSON Schema of the GRS JSON document, 'commands' the schema of the commands applyCommands takes, 'notes' the short notes to read before writing

defs.description: Names of definitions to return, as named in the schema's $defs (for example Task, Dependency); only those are returned

full.description: true returns the whole schema text, the same as the resource; it wins over defs

tools.name: readDocument
tools.description:
A frozen copy of the document with its three root groups.
By default the MSPDI pass-through fields (carry, carryElements) are left out; pass includeCarry true to keep them.
A non-empty taskUids keeps only those tasks in the six task-owned groups: tasks, assignments, taskVisuals, taskGroupMembers, taskOrigins and baselineTasks.
To get only the task group list (id, name, parent, order), pass parts ['taskGroups']: no task, calendar or resource comes with it.

includeCarry.description: Whether to keep the MSPDI pass-through fields carry and carryElements; false when omitted

taskUids.description: The uids of the tasks to read; empty or omitted reads every task

parts.description: Names of the parts to keep: keys of schedule (tasks, calendars, resources, assignments, taskGroups, taskGroupMembers, taskVisuals and the rest) and documentSettings, changeLog; an empty list keeps everything. project and documentStamp are always kept; a part left out is absent from the answer

tools.name: readStamp
tools.description:
The document stamp, for optimistic locking.
Hand it back as expectedStamp when you write.

tools.name: readSelection
tools.description: What the person has selected now, in the order it was selected.

tools.name: readSearchRows
tools.description:
Takes one word and returns the rows of the Search Panel: the task table, one page at a time, and the comment-box table.
The panel's own search field is neither read nor changed. An empty word narrows nothing, so the task rows are the whole outline.
With filters 'asShown' (the default) the column filters and sort the person has set on the task table are applied, so you get the same rows in the same order as on screen. To change them as the person would, send setTableView through applyCommands; the person's table changes too.
Up to limit task rows (at most 100) are returned from offset. The answer lists the task table's columns (id, on-screen names, value kind), the total task row count (taskTotal) and the next offset. taskTotal counts every task row the word and the filters keep, milestones and parent tasks included; a milestone row has milestone true.
Plan and actual: in a task row, plannedStart and plannedFinish are the plan (the columns Planned Start and Planned Finish; a milestone's plannedFinish is its start), and percentComplete, actualStart and actualFinish are the actual (the columns Progress, Actual Start and Actual Finish).
The status column only compares dates with the status date; for the exact delay analysis call readDelayDiagnostics.

word.description: The word to look for: a task row is kept when its task name or an assignee name holds the word, a comment box row when its text does; upper and lower case and full and half width are not told apart. An empty word narrows nothing, so the answer is the whole outline

filters.description: 'asShown' (the default) applies the column filters and sort the person has set on the Search Panel task table; 'none' applies neither

offset.description: The position of the first task row to return, from 0; 0 when omitted

limit.description: How many task rows to return; 100 when omitted, at most 100

tools.name: readTableRows
tools.description:
Returns the rows of the Delay Diagnostics Report table or the Resource List table, one page at a time, with every cell as the person sees it.
With filters 'asShown' (the default) the column filters and sort the person has set on that table are applied, so you get the same rows in the same order as on screen. The table's own search field is neither read nor changed.
The Delay Diagnostics Report table is built from a fresh diagnosis, as readDelayDiagnostics does; nothing on the screen or in the document changes.
Up to limit rows (at most 100) are returned from offset; the answer lists the columns, the total row count and the next offset.
To change a table's column filters or sort as the person would, send setTableView through applyCommands. The Search Panel is read with readSearchRows.
The fix proposals and fix log tables list the same rows readDelayDiagnostics returns in fixProposals and fixLog, as the report window shows them, a page at a time.

table.description: The table to read: the Delay Diagnostics Report table, the Resource List table, the fix proposals table or the fix log table. The two fix tables keep no column filter or sort in the document, so filters changes nothing for them

word.description: Narrows the rows the way the table's search field does; an empty word narrows nothing. To narrow by a status column (Unreliable and the like), set that column's filter with setTableView through applyCommands, then read with filters 'asShown'

filters.description: 'asShown' (the default) applies the column filters and sort the person has set on that table; 'none' applies neither

offset.description: The position of the first row to return, from 0; 0 when omitted

limit.description: How many rows to return; 100 when omitted, at most 100

tools.name: readShownTasks
tools.description:
The uids of the tasks the schedule draws now, or null when no table filters the schedule, and the names of the tables that do.
Reads only; changes neither the screen nor the document.

tools.name: readDelayDiagnostics
tools.description:
The delay diagnosis report as a frozen value: findings, unreliable values, bottlenecks and bottleneck paths, with the proposed fixes and the fix log.
Changes neither the screen nor the document.
This is the only exact delay analysis.
All amounts are working minutes. inheritedDelayMinutes is how far predecessors push the task's start; selfDelayMinutes is how far its projected finish runs past its start plus its planned length (0 for a parent task); pushOutMinutes is the part of the delay of end tasks (milestones and tasks with no successor) this task causes, summed over the terminalsReached end tasks it reaches.
terminalPushOuts holds, for each end task, terminalDelayMinutes (its projected finish past its planned finish) and givenTo (the tasks that caused it, with their minutes).
To turn minutes into days, divide by the document's project.minutesPerDay (when it is null, the value its description in the document schema gives); the screen shows a push-out rounded up to whole days.
walls lists where the diagnosis stopped, one wall per cause task: row is its kind, told by the number it ends in (1 a task whose own values contradict each other, 2 a task whose parent cannot be inferred, 3 a milestone with no predecessor); causeUid is the cause task; stoppedUids are the tasks left undiagnosed, the cause first.
A milestone that heads its own task group (no task of that task group starts on an earlier day) is the schedule's origin: it needs no predecessor and is no wall.
Two walls of the same kind differ by causeUid; their stoppedUids can be the same list, as for tasks whose dependencies form a loop.

parts.description: Names of the parts to keep (findings, bottlenecks, terminalPushOuts, walls, markerStates, settledPushOuts, derivedParentTasks, lateDays, fixProposals, fixLog); an empty list keeps everything. outcome, statusDate and unreliableCount are always kept

limit.description: The most entries returned in each list; 0 means no limit

tools.name: applyCommands
tools.description:
Writes a batch of commands atomically: every command is applied or the whole batch is refused.
Hand over the stamp you last read as expectedStamp.
The kind and the fields of every command are in the resource grs-commands.schema.json.

request.description: The stamp you last read (expectedStamp) and the batch of commands

kind.description:
The command. The keys and types of each command are in the resource grs-commands.schema.json. What each command does:
setProjectTitle: Renames the document by setting `title`.
setProjectProfile: Edits the document's basic information. `fields` holds only the fields to change; fields left out keep their current value.
setStatusDate: Sets or moves the status date to `statusDate`.
clearStatusDate: Clears the status date.
setThemeHue: Changes the theme color by setting `themeHue`.
setParentTaskProgressToleranceDays: Changes the number of days a parent task's progress may be off before it is flagged as doubtful, by setting `parentTaskProgressToleranceDays`.
setScheduleDataTimeZone: Switches the time zone of the schedule data to `scheduleDataTimeZone` without converting: the stored numbers stay the same and only the zone they are read in changes. Send it in one write together with the command that returns the shown time zone to the standard.
shiftScheduleTimes: Shifts all schedule date-times at once by `minutes` (positive moves later, negative moves earlier). It is one write; the columns it rewrites and the ones it leaves untouched are fixed by the specification. When it arrives from the Agent API, it is applied without asking the person for confirmation.
shiftScheduleToStartDate: Moves the whole schedule to start on `newStartDate`, shifting by working days. It is one write; which columns move, what stays, and how the move is made are fixed by the specification. When it arrives from the Agent API, it is applied as sent without asking, the same as `shiftScheduleTimes`.
createTask: Creates a task with the given `shapeKind`, `start` and `finish`, placed on the task group `taskGroupId`. `shapeKind` is one of `rectangle`, `chevron`, `arrow`, `endpointSpan` and `milestone`; `milestone` makes the task a milestone. The new task's uid is `project.uidHighWaterMark` plus 1, and the high-water mark moves to it, so a later command of the same batch that creates something with a uid takes the next number. Example: when `uidHighWaterMark` is 41, the batch [`createTask`, `createTask`, `setTaskName` with `taskUid` 42, `setTaskName` with `taskUid` 43] names both new tasks. A `taskGroupId` that names no task group makes a new top-level task group with that id.
deleteTask: Deletes the task `taskUid`.
pasteTasks: Duplicates the tasks listed in `sourceUids`. Descendant tasks that are not among the carried tasks are not copied. `landing` is sent only for a Ctrl-drag copy; it carries where the copy is placed.
setTaskName: Sets the name of the task `taskUid` to `name`.
setTaskNotes: Sets the notes of the task `taskUid` to `notes`.
setTaskPlanDates: Sets the planned `start` and `finish` of the task `taskUid`.
setTaskDeadline: Sets the `deadline` of the task `taskUid`.
setTaskPlanActualState: Sets the five plan-and-actual columns of the task `taskUid` as described by `place`.
beginTaskActual: Starts recording the actual of the task `taskUid` after a plan-and-actual grab handle was dragged. `grabbed` names the handle that was grabbed, `released` is where it was let go, and `snapMinutes` is the snap step in minutes that sets the length of the dummy actual.
cycleTaskPlanActualState: Advances the plan-and-actual state of the task `taskUid` by one step along the state cycle. When going back from interrupted to not started, the actual that was removed is remembered by the screen state and passed in as `remembered`. `snapMinutes` is the snap step in minutes; when left out, the day step is used.
setTaskFadeInDays: Sets the fade-in days of the task `taskUid` to `fadeInDays`.
setTaskFadeOutDays: Sets the fade-out days of the task `taskUid` to `fadeOutDays`.
setTaskParentTask: Moves the task `taskUid` under the parent task `parentTaskUid`.
moveTaskToTaskGroup: Moves the task `taskUid` to another task group `taskGroupId`.
setTaskVisualShapeKind: Changes the shape of the task `taskUid` to `shapeKind`.
setTaskVisualMilestoneGlyph: Changes the milestone shape of the task `taskUid` to `milestoneGlyph`.
setTaskVisualColors: Sets the `fillColor` and `strokeColor` of the task `taskUid`.
resetTaskVisualColors: Returns the colors of the task `taskUid` to following the theme.
setTaskVisualStrokeWidthPx: Sets the line width of the task `taskUid` to `strokeWidthPx`.
createTaskGroup: Creates a task group with the given `id`, `parentId`, `name`, `derivedFromTaskUid` and `order`.
deleteTaskGroup: Deletes the task group `taskGroupId`. Warning: the current edit does not read `newTaskGroupId`; it has no effect.
pasteTaskGroupSubtree: Duplicates the subtree of task groups rooted at `sourceTaskGroupId`, placing the copy of the root under `parentId`. `newTaskGroupIds` maps each source `id` to the `id` of its copy.
setTaskGroupName: Sets the name of the task group `taskGroupId` to `name`.
setTaskGroupColor: Sets the `color` of the task group `taskGroupId`.
resetTaskGroupColor: Returns the color of the task group `taskGroupId` to following the theme.
setTaskGroupMinHeightPx: Sets the minimum height of the task group `taskGroupId` to `minHeightPx`.
reorderTaskGroupSiblings: Reorders the sibling task groups under `parentId` (null means the top level) into the order given by `orderedIds`. That order becomes their `order`.
createDependency: Draws a dependency line from the task `predecessorUid` to the task `successorUid`. `predecessorEdge` and `successorEdge` name the ends (start or finish); the pair of ends decides the link type. If either task is a milestone, the line is always finish-to-start, whatever `predecessorEdge` and `successorEdge` say.
deleteDependency: Deletes the dependency lines from `predecessorUid` to `successorUid`. Every line in that direction is deleted; to delete only one, use `deleteDependencyAt`.
deleteDependencyAt: Deletes one dependency line among those in the same direction, named by `successorUid`, `predecessorUid` and its position `order` (0 is the first) in the successor's list of dependencies. Refused if no such line exists. Lines in the same direction have no name of their own, so the position in the list is the only way to name one.
setDependencyLag: Changes the lag of the dependency from `predecessorUid` to `successorUid`; the lag is given either as a working-day lag or as a typed lag.
setCalendar: Edits the calendar: the working weekdays, one set of working times for a working day, the exception days, and the day the week starts on. `workingDayTypes` lists the working weekdays (1 is Sunday; weekdays not listed are days off). `weekStartDay` is the day the week starts on. `exceptions` is the complete list of exception days after the edit. `workingTimes` is one set of working times for a working day. If the document still has the default calendar, create a calendar first and then edit it. The times of `fromDate` and `toDate` of an exception day are aligned by the side that writes the command into the document. `workingTimes` holds 1 to 5 spans: an empty list is refused. To go back to the default working times, pass the two default spans 08:00:00-12:00:00 and 13:00:00-17:00:00.
createResource: Adds a resource named `name`.
setResourceName: Renames the resource `resourceUid` to `name`.
deleteResources: Deletes the resources listed in `resourceUids`.
deleteUnreferencedResources: Deletes all resources that no assignment refers to.
createAssignment: Assigns the resource `resourceUid` to the task `taskUid`.
deleteAssignment: Removes the assignment of the resource `resourceUid` from the task `taskUid`.
createCommentBox: Places a comment box with the given `commentBoxId`, attached as `anchor` says. In `anchor`, leave out a key to write it as null. The snapped target (a `taskUid` with `taskFigure`, or a `highlightBoxId`) and `snapPoint` are given together, and only when the box snaps.
deleteCommentBox: Deletes the comment box `commentBoxId`.
setCommentBoxText: Sets the text of the comment box `commentBoxId` to `text`.
setCommentBoxLeaderShapeKind: Sets the leader line shape of the comment box `commentBoxId` to `leaderShapeKind`.
setCommentBoxAnchor: Changes where the comment box `commentBoxId` is attached to `anchor`. In `anchor`, leave out a key to write it as null. The snapped target (a `taskUid` with `taskFigure`, or a `highlightBoxId`) and `snapPoint` are given together, and only when the box snaps.
setCommentBoxBodyOffsetPx: Changes the offset of the body of the comment box `commentBoxId` from its anchor: `dx` is the horizontal offset in px and `dy` the vertical offset in px.
setCommentBoxStrokeColor: Sets the color of the frame and leader line of the comment box `commentBoxId` to `strokeColor`.
setCommentBoxStrokeWidthPx: Sets the width of the frame and leader line of the comment box `commentBoxId` to `strokeWidthPx`.
setCommentBoxFillColor: Sets the fill color of the body box of the comment box `commentBoxId` to `fillColor`.
setCommentBoxFillTransparencyPercent: Sets the fill transparency of the body box of the comment box `commentBoxId` to `fillTransparencyPercent`.
setCommentBoxTextColor: Sets the text color of the body of the comment box `commentBoxId` to `textColor`.
setCommentBoxFontSizePx: Sets the font size (px) of the body of the comment box `commentBoxId` to `fontSizePx`; null draws the default size.
bringCommentBoxToFront: Moves the comment box `commentBoxId` to the end of the list of comment boxes, which is the front-most position.
createHighlightBox: Places a highlight box with the given `highlightBoxId` enclosing `range`.
deleteHighlightBox: Deletes the highlight box `highlightBoxId`.
setHighlightBoxRange: Changes the area enclosed by the highlight box `highlightBoxId` to `range`.
setHighlightBoxStrokeColor: Sets the frame color of the highlight box `highlightBoxId` to `strokeColor`.
setHighlightBoxStrokeWidthPx: Sets the frame line width of the highlight box `highlightBoxId` to `strokeWidthPx`.
setHighlightBoxFillColor: Sets the fill color of the highlight box `highlightBoxId` to `fillColor`.
setHighlightBoxFillTransparencyPercent: Sets the fill transparency of the highlight box `highlightBoxId` to `fillTransparencyPercent`.
bringHighlightBoxToFront: Moves the highlight box `highlightBoxId` to the end of the list of highlight boxes, which is the front-most position.
setStackDirection: Sets the stacking direction to `stackDirection`.
setVisibilitySetting: Shows or hides one element of the screen. `setting` names the element and `isVisible` is the value to write.
setFontSizeStep: Changes the font size step to `fontSizeStep`.
setThemeMonochrome: Sets whether the theme is monochrome to `isThemeMonochrome`.
setZoom: Changes the display zoom to `zoomX` and `zoomY`.
setScrollPosition: Changes the scroll position to `scrollDate`, `scrollTaskGroupId`, `scrollDateFraction` and `scrollTaskGroupFraction`.
setTaskGroupPanelWidthPx: Changes the width of the task group panel to `taskGroupPanelWidthPx`.
pinTaskGroup: Pins the task group `taskGroupId` by adding it to the pinned task groups.
unpinTaskGroup: Unpins the task group `taskGroupId` by removing it from the pinned task groups.
fitScheduleToScreen: Sets the zoom and scroll position at which the whole schedule fits the screen: `zoomX`, `zoomY`, `scrollDate`, `scrollTaskGroupId`, `scrollDateFraction` and `scrollTaskGroupFraction`.
fitScheduleToScreenOnPage: Fits the whole schedule to the screen of the page, as the Fit button does: the page computes the zoom and the scroll position from its own screen size, so you need not know it. The page computes them from the screen as drawn before this batch, so send it in a batch of its own after the edits that change the rows. It does not unfold the task groups as the Fit button also does; to unfold them, send resetTaskGroupTreeStates in an earlier batch. It is refused while the page has not drawn its screen yet.
resetTaskGroupTreeStates: Returns the tree state of every task group to `auto`, except task groups that are hidden.
moveTaskGroup: Changes the parent and the order of the task group `taskGroupId` to `parentId` and `order`.
setDisplayScale: Changes the display scale step to `displayScale`.
setFitSpan: Sets or moves the fit span (the period shown when fitting the whole schedule), giving `fitSpanStart` and `fitSpanFinish` together.
clearFitSpan: Clears the fit span; if it was fixed, the fixing is also removed.
setFitSpanFixed: Fixes or unfixes the fit span according to `isFitSpanFixed`. If the fit span is empty, the period currently shown is copied into it: `shownStart` and `shownFinish` give that period (null when none).
setTaskGroupPanelWidthFixed: Fixes or unfixes the width of the task group panel according to `isTaskGroupPanelWidthFixed`.
setTableView: Replaces how one table looks: the displayed column values, whether the schedule filter is on, the column filters and the sort order. `table` names the table (`searchPanel`, `delayDiagnosticsReport` or `resourceList`) and `view` is the whole new view for it.
setViewTimeZone: Changes the time zone in which the schedule is shown to `viewTimeZone`; the shown times are converted accordingly. Null means the standard time row.
setDisplayTimeZones: Sets the time zones to display to `displayTimeZones` (0 to 4 of them).
setTimeOfDayVisible: Sets whether the time of day is shown to `isTimeOfDayVisible`.
setTaskGroupTreeState: Sets the tree state of the task group `taskGroupId` to `treeState`.
setTaskGroupEditPermission: Adds or removes the edit group of the task group `taskGroupId` by setting `editPermission`. Not implemented yet: refused if sent. For the person only.
setLevelZeroTreeState: Sets the tree state of level 0 to `levelZeroTreeState`.

tools.name: importDocument
tools.description:
Imports a document into the open one.
When the person must choose how (replace, add, or overlay as the baseline), the call returns at once with an ask outcome; the person's choice is then written as their own edit, so watchChanges reports it.

source.description: The document to import: the document itself, { document }, or { text } holding GRS JSON

tools.name: requestOpenFile
tools.description:
Asks the person to open a file: the page shows a question and the call returns at once.
If the person goes on, their own file window opens and they pick the file; the document they open reaches you through watchChanges as their edit.
After the person picks a file, the page asks them how to open it, with the buttons Replace, Merge and Overlay as Baseline. Tell the person to expect that question.
To know when the file is in, call watchChanges (or call readStamp until the stamp changes); then read project.title with readDocument to see which document is open.

tools.name: issueDelayFixes
tools.description:
Issues fix proposals of the Delay Diagnostics as one bundle, as the screen's Fix does: the bundle is one undo step, and if any row is refused nothing is applied.
Issued rows are recorded in the fix log (fixLog of readDelayDiagnostics) and leave the proposals table.
Unlike the screen it does not save first: the step is yours, so undoEdit takes it back; save with an export tool's fileName.
Issuing does not run the diagnosis again; call runDelayDiagnostics for that.
A recommended row can make a parent task from a task group whose tasks have none; createdUids in the answer lists the tasks it made.

expectedStamp.description: The stamp you last read; compared with the current stamp

fixKeys.description: Keys of the fix proposal rows to issue, as readDelayDiagnostics lists them in fixProposals; an empty list issues the recommended rows, as the screen's adopt-all button picks them

tools.name: undoEdit
tools.description:
Undoes the newest step of the edit history, but only a step you wrote yourself; a step the person wrote is refused with notOwnStep.
Hand over the stamp you last read as expectedStamp; a different stamp is refused with staleStamp.
A focusTask that expanded a task group wrote a step of its own: after creating a task and then calling focusTask, the first undoEdit undoes the expansion and the second the creation.

expectedStamp.description: The stamp you last read; compared with the current stamp

tools.name: redoEdit
tools.description:
Redoes the step undone last, but only a step you wrote yourself; a step the person wrote is refused with notOwnStep.
Hand over the stamp you last read as expectedStamp; a different stamp is refused with staleStamp.

expectedStamp.description: The stamp you last read; compared with the current stamp

tools.name: exportJson
tools.description:
Returns the document as GRS JSON text.
Pass fileName (ending in .json) to have the relay save it in the person's save folder instead.

tools.name: focusTask
tools.description:
Expands the task groups and ancestors the task sits in and scrolls it into view.
This is a write: when the task can only be shown by changing what is shown (expanding a collapsed task group, or showing a task a table's schedule filter hides), that change is a step of its own in the edit history, written by you. Scrolling alone adds no step.

taskUid.description: The uid of the task to show

tools.name: showOnlyTasks
tools.description:
Shows only the listed tasks: rewrites the visibility column of the Search Panel task table and turns on that table's schedule filter, as the person can.
An empty list turns the filter off and keeps the visibility values.
Opens the Search Panel minimized if it is not shown, and the page shows its band so the person sees what happened. The Delay Diagnostics Report and Resource List filters are not touched.

taskUids.description: The uids of the tasks to show; an empty list clears the filter

tools.name: runDelayDiagnostics
tools.description:
Runs the Delay Diagnostics on the screen, as the person's flame button does: it diagnoses, opens the Delay Diagnostics Report window and shows the diagnosis marks on the progress markers.
When the window is already open it runs the diagnosis again, as its Re-diagnose button does.
It changes no document, so the stamp stays and no undo step is added.
readDelayDiagnostics reads the values; this tool only shows them on the screen.

tools.name: closeWindow
tools.description:
Closes the Delay Diagnostics Report window or the Properties Panel, as its close button does.
The report window closes alone and the diagnosis marks stay on the progress markers; the Properties Panel closes as its close button closes it.
When it is already closed nothing happens. It changes no document.

which.description: What to close: the Delay Diagnostics Report window or the Properties Panel

tools.name: watchChanges
tools.description: Waits for changes confirmed by writers other than you.

waitMs.description: How long to wait, in milliseconds; when it runs out you get 'nothing yet'. Capped at 40000, below the relay's 45-second deadline
